learning: If max_error falls below 0.06 m without steering_oscillation rising above about 0.15, narrowing is working and the next step is wheel_track 0.08 m. If steering_oscillation rises, lower kp to about 1.3 before reverting geometry, since the extra turn rate is the likely cause.
notes: Iteration 1 controller and body unchanged, with only wheel_track narrowed from 0.12 to 0.09 m. This isolates the turn-authority test the Builder requested. Controller errors and noise robustness are added to the measurements to check the controller under the new turn rate.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 is still the best layout (55.1). In every iteration all 180 development trials ended off_track, with progress 0.10 to 0.16 and max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Iteration 2 showed that moving the sensors to y=0.07 and cutting body length and mass lowered the score to 47.8, so the Builder's revert to the iteration 1 sensor layout is correct. The Builder's single change is wheel_track 0.12 to 0.09 m. Turn rate is (vR-vL)/wheel_track, so the same PWM differential turns about 1.33x faster. I therefore keep the iteration 1 controller unchanged (base_speed 1.5, kp 1.5, ki 0.02, kd 0.25, weights proportional to sensor x, last_direction). This isolates the geometry change, so any shift in max_error, steering_oscillation or line loss can be attributed to wheel_track. The one risk is that the higher effective turn gain raises steering_oscillation, which was already about 0.15 on the s-bend and slalom in iteration 1. If that happens in the next race, the fix is controller-side (lower kp) rather than more geometry. Expected result: max_error and rms_error fall on the s-bend and slalom, with line loss at or below iteration 1. This is a prediction, not a measurement.
